content.title: About
content.content: The bison is a large herbivorous mammal from the bovine family native to North America. Bison meat is rich in protein, iron, zinc and B‑vitamins, has a mild flavor and relatively low fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Adult male bison can weigh up to 1,000 kg, females up to 600 kg.
In the 19th century fewer than 1,000 bison remained in the United States; thanks to conservation their numbers have risen to over 500,000 today.
Bison meat is considered more diet‑friendly than beef, containing about 40 % less fat and calories.
Bison can run up to 35 mph (56 km/h) but usually travel at 5–10 mph (8–16 km/h).
Native American peoples traditionally used bison meat for dried steaks and hearty soups.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Bison provides about 22 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with beef, bison contains roughly half the saturated fat, which is better for heart health.

items.title: High iron content
items.content: The iron in bison meat is highly bioavailable and helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Zinc and vitamin B12
items.content: Zinc supports immune function, while vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Bison meat does not cause rapid spikes in blood sugar, making it suitable for people managing diabetes.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bison meat.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels can exacerbate gout symptoms; those with gout should limit intake.

items.title: Product quality
items.content: Purchase bison from reputable sources to avoid contamination with bacteria or hormones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bison can be prepared like beef: grill steaks, braise in stews, roast in the oven, or use ground bison for burgers and meatballs. For extra tenderness, marinate for 1–2 hours in olive oil with herbs before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh bison meat refrigerated at 0–4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken empanada is a traditional Spanish‑Latin American pastry made from a thin dough shell filled with seasoned ground chicken, spices, and sometimes vegetables. The crust is crisp, while the filling is juicy and aromatic, making it a popular snack or light meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Empanadas originated in Spain and quickly spread throughout Latin America, where each region added its own twist.
Chicken in empanadas is often seasoned with paprika, cumin, and garlic, giving it a distinctive flavor.
The dough can be baked or fried; fried empanadas are crunchier, baked ones are less fatty.
In Argentina empanadas are commonly served with chimichurri sauce, while in Chile they are paired with a spicy piri‑piri sauce.
Empanadas are convenient to take on the go, making them a popular street food and travel snack.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken meat supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Moderate carbohydrate content
items.content: The thin wheat dough contributes a moderate amount of carbs, making the empanada suitable for balanced eating.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Chicken delivers iron and zinc, important for immune function and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Paprika, garlic and other spices add antioxidant compounds that help protect cells.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The wheat dough can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt and soy‑based sauces can raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella; ensure the empanada is cooked through.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Fried empanadas are higher in calories due to oil; portion control is advisable for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken empanada can be enjoyed hot or warm as a standalone snack, or with chimichurri, salsa, or a yogurt dip. Its handheld shape makes it ideal for picnics and on‑the‑go meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked empanadas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag; reheat in the oven or microwave until the crust is crisp before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: The Ham Sandwich Wrap is a ready‑to‑eat roll filled with sliced ham, cheese, fresh vegetables and sauce, all wrapped in a soft flatbread. It’s convenient for a quick snack or lunch, providing protein, carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ham sandwich wrap appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a fast‑food alternative.
Cheddar cheese is often used, giving the wrap a distinctive flavor and meltable texture.
The wrap is portable and can be eaten without utensils.
Variations may include avocado, cherry tomatoes, or spinach leaves.
A vegetarian version replaces ham with smoked tofu.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham and cheese provide complete proteins essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat products like ham are good sources of heme iron, which supports oxygen transport.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham and whole‑grain flatbread supply B12 and other B‑vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain flatbread contribute fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ham is often high in salt, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and ham may contain saturated fats that should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy proteins should avoid wraps containing cheese.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Pre‑made wraps can contain preservatives and stabilizers that may cause sensitivity in some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The wrap can be eaten cold, sliced in half, or lightly warmed in a microwave or skillet. It pairs well with a fruit salad or a light yogurt dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the wrap in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C, wrapped in plastic film or in an airtight container. Consume within 2–3 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Fat‑free evaporated milk is a concentrated dairy product made by removing almost all fat and then evaporating water. The result is a thick, sweet product high in protein and calcium but without fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fat‑free evaporated milk is popular in diet nutrition because it retains sweetness without added fat.
Unlike regular evaporated milk, it contains about 0.1 % fat.
The high sugar concentration allows it to be stored for long periods without refrigeration.
In many countries it serves as a base for desserts, sauces, and beverages.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: It provides roughly 8 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Contains about 120 mg of calcium per 100 g, important for bone health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of fat makes it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides riboflavin (B2) and B12, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Without fat, it is gentle on the digestive system, useful for people with gastrointestinal sensitivities.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The product is very sweet; people with diabetes or those watching their weight should limit intake.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains lactose, so it is unsuitable for those who cannot digest it.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey may react.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use fat‑free evaporated milk in desserts, porridge, smoothies, sauces, and baked goods. It can be reconstituted with water for a light milk drink or added to coffee for sweetness without fat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 2–3 days.
